benefit.name: Optical Supplements (Glasses & Eye Exams)
benefit.amount: Routine eye exam up to $44.83 with an optometrist or $48.90 with an ophthalmologist once every 2 years; new prescription glasses at the ministry's maximum rates, plus new lenses if your eye doctor confirms a change in your prescription
benefit.summary: Eye exams and prescription eyewear for everyone on income or disability assistance. Show your BC Services Card at any eye clinic, and the ministry pays the optometrist or optician directly.
benefit.note: MSP already covers children's routine eye exams. The supplement pays for their glasses. You may be responsible for costs above the ministry's fee schedule, so ask the clinic first.

detail.about: Everyone receiving income or disability assistance gets specified optical services: routine eye exams for adults ($44.83 with an optometrist or $48.90 with an ophthalmologist every two years), new eyeglasses up to ministry maximum rates, new lenses if your eye doctor confirms a change in your prescription, and necessary repairs to lenses or frames. Payment goes straight from the ministry to the optometrist or optician.

steps: Take your BC Services Card to any eye clinic
The clinic verifies your coverage through Pacific Blue Cross
Get your exam and choose frames within the ministry rate (or pay the difference)
The ministry pays the provider directly
tips: Ask the clinic which frames are fully covered at ministry rates before choosing
If your eye doctor confirms a change in your prescription, new lenses are covered
detail.time: No application — coverage verified at the clinic on the spot
